tool.name: pyrho compute_r2
tool.description: Compute theoretical quantiles/mean of the r^2 distribution

param.name: tablefile
param.label: pyrho lookup table
param.help: The demography-specific lookup table produced by pyrho make_table.

param.name: samplesize
param.label: Sample size (number of haplotypes)
param.help: The number of haplotypes to compute the r^2 distribution for. Must be no larger than the lookup table sample size.

param.name: MAFcut
param.label: Minor allele frequency cutoff
param.help: Only pairs of sites where both sites have a minor allele frequency above this threshold are considered. Must be less than 0.5.

param.name: compute_mean
param.label: Compute the mean of r^2
param.help: Also compute the mean of the r^2 distribution.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`pyrho compute_r2` computes the theoretical quantiles and/or mean of the distribution of the linkage disequilibrium measure r^2 from a lookup table. This can be used to check whether an inferred demography or recombination map fits the data well, since the distribution of r^2 depends heavily on the demographic history.
**Inputs**
- **Lookup table** — the HDF5 output of `pyrho make_table`. - **Sample size** — the number of haplotypes for which to compute the distribution. Must be no larger than the lookup table sample size. - **MAF cutoff** — only pairs of sites where both sites have a minor allele frequency above this threshold are considered. - **Quantiles** — comma-delimited list of quantiles to compute. - **Compute mean** — also compute the mean of the r^2 distribution.
**Output**
A tabular file with a `r` column (the recombination rate rho) and optional `mean` and quantile columns.
**Notes**
- The distribution of r^2 is very sensitive to low-frequency alleles, which are also the most difficult to genotype accurately. Use `--MAFcut` to condition on minor allele frequency.
